title: User Account and Access Management Policy
text: All employees and approved contractors must use an individual account to access company systems, project repositories, hosting dashboards, and client workspaces. Shared accounts are prohibited because they make activity difficult to trace. A team lead must submit an access request that identifies the person, required systems, business purpose, and expected access period. The system owner approves permissions according to the principle of least privilege. Multi-factor authentication must be enabled wherever available. When a person changes roles or leaves the organization, the manager must request a review or removal of access before the final working day. Access rights are reviewed every quarter, and unusual login activity must be reported to the security contact.

title: Website Change and Release Management Procedure
text: Every change to a production website must be recorded in the change log before implementation. The request must describe the affected page or service, the reason for the change, expected impact, responsible developer, and planned release window. Changes are reviewed by a second team member and tested in a staging environment using the agreed acceptance criteria. The release owner confirms that a recent backup exists and that a rollback method is documented. High-impact changes require approval from the service owner before deployment. After release, the team checks page availability, forms, navigation, and key integrations. The change record is closed only after the result and any follow-up work are documented.

title: Incident Reporting and Escalation Procedure
text: Any employee who identifies a service interruption, security concern, or significant defect must create an incident record in the support queue. The record should include the affected website or system, time first observed, symptoms, user impact, screenshots or error messages, and actions already attempted. The support coordinator assigns a severity level based on scope and business impact. Critical incidents affecting many users or exposing information are immediately escalated to the technical lead and service owner. The assigned responder posts status updates at agreed intervals and records decisions in the same ticket. Once service is restored, the incident owner documents the cause, resolution, and preventive actions before closing the record.

title: Backup and Recovery Standard
text: Production website files, databases, configuration files, and essential design assets must be backed up on a documented schedule. The service owner defines backup frequency according to the importance and update rate of each service. Backups must be encrypted, stored separately from the production environment, and accessible only to authorized personnel. The operations team checks backup jobs for failures and records the result of each review. A recovery test must be performed at least every six months and after major infrastructure changes. The test records the recovery time, data completeness, problems encountered, and corrective actions. A backup is not considered reliable until a restoration has been successfully demonstrated.

title: Code Review and Quality Assurance Workflow
text: Code that changes a website or shared component must be reviewed by another qualified team member before it is merged into the main branch. The author links the change to its task, explains the intended behavior, and identifies affected pages, APIs, or dependencies. Reviewers check readability, security, accessibility, responsive behavior, and consistency with established components. Automated tests should run before approval, while visual changes must also be checked at common desktop and mobile widths. Review comments are resolved or explicitly discussed before merging. The person responsible for the release records the test outcome and verifies the change in staging. Urgent fixes may use an expedited review, but the review must still be documented.

title: Client Onboarding and Project Handover Process
text: At the start of a website project, the project coordinator collects the client's goals, target audience, required pages, functional needs, brand assets, accessibility expectations, and approval contacts. The team confirms the scope, responsibilities, communication channel, and method for submitting change requests. Designers document approved visual references and explain important interface decisions. Developers record the technology stack, integrations, hosting arrangements, and deployment dependencies. Before handover, the project team provides the client with administrator instructions, known limitations, maintenance contacts, and a list of outstanding tasks. The client representative confirms receipt, and the coordinator stores the final documents in the shared project repository so future support staff can find them.

title: Data Handling and Retention Policy
text: Project teams must collect and retain only the information needed to deliver and support a digital service. Client files, exported user records, credentials, and diagnostic logs must be stored in approved locations rather than personal devices or unapproved file-sharing services. Sensitive information must be protected with appropriate access controls and encryption during transfer and storage. The project owner classifies records according to their purpose and retention period. When a contract ends or a retention period expires, the responsible team securely deletes or returns the information according to the service agreement and applicable requirements. Deletion actions involving production data must be recorded, and suspected exposure or loss must be reported through the incident process.

title: Website Performance Review Procedure
text: The operations team reviews website performance on a regular schedule and after releases that affect images, scripts, stylesheets, databases, or hosting configuration. The review considers page loading time, server response time, error rate, resource usage, and performance on mobile connections. Measurements are compared with the service baseline and the targets agreed with the client. When results exceed a threshold, the owner records the affected pages, likely contributing resources, and proposed corrective action. Optimization work may include image compression, caching, reducing unnecessary scripts, database indexing, or hosting adjustments. The team repeats the measurements after changes and adds the findings to the service history for future planning.

title: Design Approval and Accessibility Checklist
text: A website interface must receive design approval before implementation begins. The design owner shares the prototype, page structure, reusable components, responsive states, and notes explaining important interaction decisions. Reviewers assess whether navigation is understandable, text is readable, controls have clear labels, and color contrast is sufficient. The team checks keyboard navigation, focus visibility, alternative text for meaningful images, and form error messages. Client feedback is recorded with the decision made for each requested change. Approved designs are versioned and stored with the project documentation. If implementation requires a deviation, the developer records the reason and obtains approval from the design owner so the delivered interface remains consistent with the agreed experience.

title: Third-Party Service and Dependency Review
text: Before a project adopts a third-party plugin, library, API, analytics service, or hosting integration, the technical owner reviews its purpose, maintenance status, security history, licensing, and effect on site performance. The review identifies the data exchanged with the provider and the permissions required by the integration. Dependencies must be obtained from trusted sources and recorded with their versions. The team avoids unnecessary packages and plans updates for components that receive security fixes. A dependency change is tested in staging to identify compatibility problems with the content management system, theme, forms, and other plugins. The decision, selected version, and any known risks are documented for future maintenance.

title: Service Monitoring and Maintenance Schedule
text: Each production service must have an assigned owner and a maintenance schedule covering availability checks, certificate expiration, domain renewal, software updates, storage capacity, and critical integrations. Monitoring alerts should identify the affected service, time of failure, and relevant metric so responders can investigate without repeating basic checks. The operations team reviews alerts for recurring patterns and adjusts thresholds when they create noise or fail to detect meaningful problems. Planned maintenance is announced to affected stakeholders with the expected impact and recovery window. Completed maintenance is recorded with the actions performed, validation results, and any remaining risks. Repeated failures are reviewed during the service meeting and may result in a corrective project.

title: Content Publishing and Approval Workflow
text: Content editors must prepare and review website text, images, links, and downloadable files before publishing them to a live page. Each item is checked for accuracy, spelling, appropriate permissions, descriptive headings, useful alternative text, and working links. Content that includes prices, legal statements, service commitments, or personal information requires approval from the designated subject owner. The editor previews the page on desktop and mobile and confirms that the layout remains readable. Scheduled publication dates and the person approving the content are recorded in the content log. When published content is corrected or removed, the editor documents the reason and verifies that navigation, search results, and related links no longer point to outdated information.

title: Knowledge Base and Support Documentation Standard
text: Technical teams must document recurring support problems, verified workarounds, configuration steps, and lessons learned in the shared knowledge base. An article should have a clear title, affected service, symptoms, diagnostic steps, confirmed resolution, owner, and last-reviewed date. Writers must distinguish tested instructions from assumptions and avoid including passwords, personal data, or confidential client information. Similar articles should be linked rather than copied without context. The support lead reviews frequently used articles and updates them when software versions or service configurations change. When a ticket is resolved using an existing article, the responder records whether the instructions were accurate. This feedback helps the organization keep support knowledge reliable and reusable.

title: Website Login Failure After Password Reset
text: Several users reported that they could not sign in to the client portal after completing the password reset process. The reset page displayed a success message, but the new password was rejected on the login screen. Support confirmed that the issue affected accounts created before the latest authentication update and did not affect newly registered users. The responder checked the authentication logs and found that an older password-hash setting was still being used for a subset of accounts. The configuration was corrected and affected users were asked to reset their passwords once more. Login was tested with representative accounts, and the ticket was closed after users confirmed access. The team added a regression test for password reset and login compatibility.

title: Production Website Returns Intermittent Server Errors
text: The monitoring service detected intermittent server errors on the main website during a period of increased traffic. Visitors sometimes received an error page when opening product and contact pages, while other requests completed normally. Support reviewed application logs and observed that database connections were reaching the configured limit. The operations responder identified several long-running queries introduced by a recent reporting feature. The team temporarily reduced the reporting workload, restarted the affected application workers, and confirmed that page requests were completing successfully. Developers later optimized the queries and added an alert for connection-pool saturation. The incident record includes the affected time window, user impact, mitigation, permanent fix, and follow-up monitoring task.

title: Contact Form Submissions Are Not Reaching the Support Inbox
text: A client reported that messages sent through the website contact form were not arriving in the support inbox. The form displayed a confirmation message, so visitors believed their requests had been received. Support submitted test messages and found that the website stored each submission but the outgoing email service rejected delivery because its authentication token had expired. The operations team renewed the token, checked the sender configuration, and sent a test message to multiple recipients. Previously stored submissions were exported and delivered to the support team for manual follow-up. The responder verified a new form submission from desktop and mobile and documented the recovery. A reminder was added to review integration credentials before expiration.

title: Mobile Navigation Menu Does Not Open
text: Users reported that the navigation menu on the mobile version of a website stopped opening after a front-end update. The menu button remained visible, but tapping it produced no change and visitors could not reach secondary pages on smaller screens. Support reproduced the problem on two mobile browsers and confirmed that desktop navigation still worked. Inspection showed that a JavaScript event handler was attached to an outdated button identifier after a shared component had been renamed. The developer restored the correct event binding, checked keyboard activation, and tested the menu at several screen widths. The release was deployed after review, and the support ticket recorded the affected component, root cause, tested browsers, and verification results.

title: Expired SSL Certificate Causes Browser Security Warning
text: Visitors began seeing a browser security warning when opening the organization's customer website. The site was reachable, but the browser indicated that the secure connection could not be trusted. Support checked the certificate details and confirmed that the TLS certificate had expired overnight. The operations team renewed the certificate through the hosting provider, installed the updated chain, and verified the domain using more than one browser. The team also checked that HTTP requests redirected to HTTPS and that no mixed-content warnings appeared on key pages. Service was restored after the certificate changes propagated. The incident report notes the expiration time, renewal steps, validation evidence, and a new monitoring alert set to notify the owner before the next expiration date.

title: Website Pages Load Slowly on Mobile Connections
text: A client observed that the home page and service catalog took much longer to load on mobile networks than on office Wi-Fi. Support measured the pages and found that several large hero images and an uncompressed promotional video were downloaded before the main content appeared. The team also identified scripts from an unused marketing widget. The front-end developer compressed and resized the images, delayed the video until requested, and removed the unused script after client approval. Performance measurements improved on mobile devices, and the team checked that image quality and page layout remained acceptable. The ticket includes before-and-after measurements and recommends adding a media-size check to the publishing process.

title: Broken Layout Following Content Management System Update
text: After a scheduled content management system update, several pages displayed overlapping text and incorrectly sized buttons. The problem was most visible on tablet screens and affected pages using an older custom theme. Support compared the affected pages with the staging environment and found that the update changed a default style rule used by the theme. The team restored the previous theme version as a temporary measure, then updated the component styles to match the new system behavior. Regression checks were completed on common screen sizes and key templates before the corrected theme was released. The incident record links the update, affected templates, rollback, permanent correction, and compatibility test results.

title: Unexpected 404 Errors on Recently Published Pages
text: Visitors received not-found errors when following links to pages that had been published earlier in the day. The content team could open the pages from the administration panel, but public links returned a 404 response. Support checked the page status, URL structure, and server rewrite rules. The investigation found that a permalink setting had changed during a configuration update, leaving the routing cache with outdated paths. The responder refreshed the routing rules and cleared the relevant cache, then tested the affected URLs and internal navigation. The pages became available without restoring the content. The ticket documents the changed setting and adds a post-update check for public page URLs.

title: Database Connection Failure Prevents Portal Access
text: Employees were unable to open the internal project portal and received a message indicating that the application could not connect to its database. The service dashboard showed that the database server was online, but the application logs contained repeated authentication failures. The responder discovered that a database password had been rotated without updating the production application's secret configuration. The operations team updated the stored credential through the approved secret-management process and restarted the application service. Access was then tested with several user roles, and monitoring confirmed that connection errors had stopped. The incident was linked to the credential-rotation change, and the team added a deployment checklist item to verify dependent services after secret updates.

title: Suspicious Administrator Login Requires Security Review
text: The security monitor generated an alert after an administrator account attempted to sign in from an unfamiliar location and triggered multiple failed authentication attempts. The support responder contacted the account owner through a verified channel and temporarily disabled the account while the activity was reviewed. Audit logs showed no successful changes to website content or configuration, but the password may have been exposed. The team revoked active sessions, issued a credential reset, confirmed multi-factor authentication, and reviewed other administrator accounts for similar activity. The account was re-enabled after the owner completed verification. The incident record preserves relevant timestamps and actions without storing the password, and a follow-up task was created to review administrator access.

title: Third-Party Map Widget Stops Displaying on Service Pages
text: A client reported that the location map had disappeared from several service pages even though the surrounding page content loaded normally. Support reproduced the issue and found an authorization error in the browser console when the page requested map data. The provider had introduced a new API-key restriction, while the website was still using the previous configuration. The integration owner reviewed the provider settings, registered the production domain, and updated the key using the approved configuration process. The team verified that maps loaded on desktop and mobile and confirmed that unrelated forms and page scripts continued to work. The incident notes the external dependency, configuration change, validation steps, and need to monitor provider announcements.

title: Recent Backup Cannot Be Restored During Recovery Test
text: During a scheduled recovery exercise, the operations team found that the most recent website backup could not be restored because the archive was incomplete. The backup job had reported success, but a storage transfer interruption had left out several uploaded media files. The team located the previous verified backup and restored the test environment from that copy, then compared database records and media assets to identify the missing content. No production data was lost because the issue was discovered during testing. Operations corrected the transfer retry settings, added an archive-integrity check, and ran a second restoration successfully. The incident record includes the failed job, recovery decision, validation results, and actions to prevent an undetected incomplete backup.
